<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule VII - Classification of Occupancy">


BOARD EXAM WARNING:
The Philippine Code uses Roman numerals I–V for Types of Construction, but **Type I is the least fire-resistive and Type V is the most fire-resistive**, the reverse of the common US practice.[file:17]


</LawCallout>

Question 1 — Occupancy and Construction Type
An architect is designing a 5-storey shopping mall in Cebu City using reinforced concrete with a fire-resistive structural system. Under PD 1096, what are the correct Occupancy Group and Construction Type?

A) Group M (Mercantile), Type I
B) Group E (Business and Mercantile), Type V
C) Group C (Education and Recreation), Type IV
D) Group E (Business and Mercantile), Type I

Correct Answer: B

A mall is a retail/business occupancy → **Group E (Business and Mercantile)**.[file:17]
Reinforced concrete with a fire-resistive rating corresponds to the **most fire-resistive** type → **Type V** in PD 1096.[file:17]
Group M does not exist in PD 1096; Type I is wood construction, not fire-resistive.[file:17]

Question 2 — The 10-Person Threshold
A convent houses 12 nuns on a non-leasing basis. Under PD 1096/IRR, what is the occupancy group?

A) Group A, Div. 1
B) Group A, Div. 2
C) Group B
D) Group D, Div. 1

Correct Answer: C

Group A Div. 2 includes convents/monasteries for non-leasing occupants **not exceeding 10 persons**.[file:17]
When such a building accommodates **more than 10 persons**, it is classified under **Group B (Residentials, Hotels and Apartments)**.[file:17]

blocks.raw:
Question 3 — Type II vs Type III
What is the key distinction between Type II and Type III construction in PD 1096?

A) Type II uses masonry; Type III uses wood.
B) Both are roughly 1-hour fire-resistive, but Type III requires incombustible exterior walls.
C) Type II is fully incombustible; Type III allows wood framing.
D) Type III has 2-hour fire rating; Type II has 1-hour.

Correct Answer: B

Type II = wood construction with fire-resistive treatment (approx. 1-hour), exterior walls may still be wood within limits.[file:17]
Type III = masonry and wood construction, also ~1-hour, but exterior walls must be of incombustible fire-resistive construction.[file:17]

blocks.raw:
Question 4 — Mixed Occupancy Exception
A one-storey building contains a convenience store and a barber shop (both Group E) with no separation. Under Sec. 703, which rule applies?

A) The most restrictive occupancy governs the entire building.
B) Each portion may be treated under its own occupancy requirements because the building is one storey.
C) The larger occupancy governs because it exceeds 10% of total area.
D) The building must be reclassified as Group H due to public traffic.

Correct Answer: B

Sec. 703 Exception (a) allows one-storey mixed-occupancy buildings to have each portion conform to its own occupancy requirements, rather than defaulting to the most restrictive group.[file:17]
